items.headline: Wall Street Reacts to Fed Rate Hike Amid Easing Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. equities closed higher today as the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point, the first hike since July 2023, to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%. The decision was unanimous, signaling the Fed's commitment to combating inflation, which has been exacerbated by elevated energy prices and geopolitical tensions. Easing oil prices provided some relief, while stronger-than-expected August retail sales suggested underlying economic resilience.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Raises Key Interest Rate to Combat Inflation
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) unanimously voted to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75% to 4.00% today. This marks the first rate hike since July 2023, reflecting the central bank's aggressive stance against persistent inflation. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting commentary and the Summary of Economic Projections will be closely scrutinized for future policy direction.

items.headline: Technology and Industrials Lead Gains, Energy Lags Amid Oil Price Easing
items.summary: Today saw Technology and Industrials sectors leading the market, each advancing by 0.9%. Conversely, the Energy sector was the weakest performer, declining by 2.3% as crude oil prices retreated. Consumer Discretionary, Utilities, and Consumer Staples also faced pressure.

items.headline: Strong Retail Sales Signal Economic Resilience
items.summary: A report released this morning indicated that U.S. retail sales in August significantly exceeded economists' expectations. This robust consumer spending data suggests the economy remains strong enough to absorb higher interest rates.

items.headline: Dollarama Reports Strong Q2 Results; FedEx Expected to Report
items.summary: Dollarama Inc. ($DOL) announced impressive second-quarter fiscal 2027 results, with sales up 17.6% and diluted earnings per share increasing by 11.2%. Planet Image International ($YIBO) also released its Q2 2026 earnings. Investors are awaiting earnings reports from other companies, including FedEx.
